title: What If You Got 2x Heavier Every Single Day?

shots.line: Day seven.

shots.line: and your shoe sinks into the road

shots.line: What if you got two times heavier... every single day?
shots.scene: TITLE: you on a cracking road at golden hour, the ground bending under you; WHAT IF YOU GOT 2× HEAVIER EVERY DAY?

shots.line: It starts on a Monday.
shots.scene: ESTABLISH: bright bathroom morning, MON; you step onto the scale

shots.line: You step on the bathroom scale, and it says one hundred and forty kilos.
shots.scene: INSERT: the scale digits roll up to 140 kg

shots.line: Yesterday, it said seventy.
shots.scene: INSERT: a ghost 70 kg crossed out; SUN on the calendar

shots.line: Your mom says the scale is broken.
shots.scene: MEDIUM: Mom taps the scale and shrugs

shots.line: So you buy a new one.
shots.scene: INSERT: a new scale box opens

shots.line: It says the same thing.
shots.scene: INSERT: the new scale says 140 kg too; your deadpan feet

shots.line: You look exactly the same.
shots.scene: BIG FACE in the bathroom mirror, unchanged

shots.line: Same size.
shots.scene: MEDICAL CHART UI: HEIGHT 172 cm ✓, X-RAY normal ✓

shots.line: Same face.
shots.scene: MEDICAL CHART UI: WEIGHT 140 kg ⚠ ?!

shots.line: You can still walk, run and jump like always.
shots.scene: LIVING ROOM: you jump, the landing cracks the floor tiles

shots.line: Your body keeps up.
shots.scene: BIG FACE: you grin, flex

shots.line: Everything else doesn't.
shots.scene: INSERT: a chair splits under you

shots.line: Because every night, at the stroke of midnight, your weight doubles.
shots.scene: NIGHT bedroom: midnight clock, ×2 stamp glows

shots.line: Day one, you weigh as much as a gorilla.
shots.scene: WEIGHT LADDER: a seesaw, you vs a gorilla; the gorilla flies up; DAY 1 140 kg

shots.line: Day two, a piano.
shots.scene: SEESAW: you vs a piano; DAY 2 280 kg

shots.line: Day four, a car.
shots.scene: SEESAW: you vs a car; DAY 4 1,120 kg

shots.scene: SEESAW: you vs a T. rex; DAY 7 8,960 kg

shots.line: At first, it's kind of awesome.
shots.scene: BIG FACE: grinning, thumbs up

shots.line: Nobody can push you over.
shots.scene: SCHOOL HALL: a big kid shoves you and bounces off

shots.line: In gym class, the whole team pulls on the other end of the rope...
shots.scene: GYM: the whole class pulls the rope against you

shots.line: and you don't move an inch.
shots.scene: CLOSE: your feet planted; the coach's whistle drops from his mouth

shots.line: But there's one person you really want to show.
shots.scene: you pick up a framed photo

shots.line: Your grandpa.
shots.scene: INSERT photo: you and Grandpa at the lake, red lifeguard jacket

shots.line: Every summer since you were five, he's taken you to the lake.
shots.scene: SEPIA flashback: summer lake, the dock, little you and Grandpa

shots.line: He used to be a lifeguard.
shots.scene: SEPIA: young Grandpa on a lifeguard chair, whistle

shots.line: He's the one who taught you to float.
shots.scene: SEPIA: Grandpa in the water, little you on your back

shots.line: "Lie back. Spread your arms.
shots.scene: SEPIA BIG FACE: Grandpa, warm sun — his line

shots.line: Trust the water. It'll hold you up."
shots.scene: SEPIA: little you floating, arms spread, Grandpa's hand lets go

shots.line: So on day three, you run to the end of the dock,
shots.scene: PRESENT: you run down the dock, Grandpa on the shore; DAY 3

shots.line: and you jump.
shots.scene: you mid-air off the end of the dock

shots.line: And you sink.
shots.scene: UNDERWATER: you plunge like a stone, a column of bubbles

shots.line: Straight to the bottom.
shots.scene: you thud onto the lakebed, a sand cloud

shots.line: Five meters down, you look up at the light...
shots.scene: LOOKING UP from the bottom: bright surface, light rays

shots.line: and then you walk out of the lake, along the bottom.
shots.scene: CUT-AWAY of the lake: you walk up the slope along the bottom

shots.line: Grandpa doesn't say a word.
shots.scene: SHORE: you come out dripping; Grandpa frozen

shots.line: He just wraps a towel around your shoulders.
shots.scene: Grandpa wraps a towel around your shoulders

shots.line: The water doesn't hold you up anymore.
shots.scene: BIG FACE: wet, sad, the towel

shots.line: Day four, the stairs give way under your feet.
shots.scene: STAIRS: the steps snap under you; DAY 4

shots.scene: CUTAWAY house: the bed crashes from the bedroom into the kitchen

shots.line: Day six, you're as heavy as an elephant.
shots.scene: DAY 6: an elephant on the seesaw = you

shots.line: Your best friend ties a rope from you to his dad's pickup truck,
shots.scene: STREET: your friend ties a rope from you to his dad's pickup

shots.line: The tires scream.
shots.scene: CLOSE: spinning tires, smoke

shots.line: The truck shakes.
shots.scene: the truck shudders, rope taut

shots.line: You don't move.
shots.scene: you, calm, sipping a juice box

shots.line: They call you the Immovable Kid.

shots.scene: TOP VIEW: a trail of deep footprints in the road; DAY 7

shots.line: Cars can't carry you.

shots.line: Buses can't carry you.

shots.line: The city lays steel plates on the sidewalk, just for you.

shots.line: Day eight, you're as heavy as a fire truck.
shots.scene: DAY 8: a fire truck on the seesaw = you

shots.line: Your school asks you to stay home.
shots.scene: EMAIL UI from school: Please stay home

shots.line: Not for you.

shots.line: And day nine...
shots.scene: DUSK river; DAY 9

shots.line: the bridge.
shots.scene: the bridge, long lens

shots.line: Your grandpa lives on the other side of the river.
shots.scene: Grandpa's house across the river, porch light on

shots.line: The sign says ten tonnes.
shots.scene: INSERT: 10 t sign

shots.line: You weigh thirty-six, as much as a fully loaded eighteen-wheeler.
shots.scene: 36 t: an 18-wheeler on the seesaw = you

shots.line: So he calls you every night.
shots.scene: VIDEO CALL UI: Grandpa on the phone; you small in the corner

shots.line: And every night, he asks the same thing.
shots.scene: GARAGE night: you on the floor, phone glow

shots.line: "You still floating, kiddo?"

shots.line: She shows you what happens next.

shots.line: Day fourteen, even solid rock can't hold you.
shots.scene: CUT-AWAY of the ground: you sinking into bedrock; DAY 14

shots.line: You'll sink into the ground with every step.
shots.scene: each step punches a hole, you knee-deep

shots.line: Day thirty-one, you'll pull on anything a meter away as hard as the whole Earth does.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: you, pebbles pulled toward you, 1 g at 1 m; DAY 31

shots.line: The ground will start falling in on you.
shots.scene: CUT-AWAY: rock caving in around you

shots.line: Day seventy-seven, you'll weigh more than the planet.
shots.scene: BALANCE: you vs the Earth, the Earth goes up; DAY 77

shots.line: "You can't stay on Earth. And after tomorrow, no rocket can lift you."
shots.scene: BIG FACE: Dr. Voss, cold light — her line

shots.line: Atlas has one rocket big enough.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: the Atlas rocket

shots.line: It can carry a hundred tonnes.
shots.scene: PAYLOAD BAR: limit 100 t

shots.line: Tomorrow, you'll weigh seventy-two.
shots.scene: PAYLOAD BAR: 72 t fits ✓

shots.line: The day after, a hundred and forty-three.

shots.scene: COUNTDOWN UI: LAUNCH TOMORROW 23:00

shots.line: Before midnight.
shots.scene: INSERT: midnight clock, red

shots.scene: BIG FACE: you, the floodlight on your face

shots.line: You have one day left on Earth.
shots.scene: GARAGE: you sitting on the floor, alone

shots.line: And there's one person you need to see.
shots.scene: INSERT: the photo of you and Grandpa on the garage wall

shots.line: Up there, everything floats."

shots.scene: silence in the capsule

shots.line: And you float.
shots.scene: you lift off the seat

shots.scene: you floating, a smile

shots.line: You lie back.
shots.scene: you lie back in the air

shots.line: You spread your arms.
shots.scene: arms spread, the Earth in the window

shots.line: Somewhere down there, your grandpa is looking up.
shots.scene: NIGHT: Grandpa on his porch looks up at a moving star

shots.line: So, is any of this real?
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: IS ANY OF THIS REAL?

shots.line: Not the doubling.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: the doubling curve crossed out

shots.line: And in real life, your body wouldn't keep up.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: body outline, heart

shots.line: Fighter pilots in tight turns can feel nine times their own weight,
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: a jet in a tight turn, 9 g

shots.line: and even they need special suits and training not to black out.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: pilot in a G-suit

shots.line: At eight times your weight, on day three, your heart couldn't push blood up to your brain.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: heart pumping blood up to the brain fails, 8×

shots.line: You'd faint.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: outline faints, eyes X

shots.line: Floors have limits too.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: floor beam

shots.line: A normal house floor is built for about two hundred kilos on every square meter.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: a 1 m² tile, 200 kg

shots.line: On day five, your bed puts five times that on it.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: the bed, 1,000 kg on every m², ×5, beam cracks

shots.line: You float because, with air in your lungs, your body is a tiny bit lighter than the same amount of water.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: water tank, a body floats (air in lungs)

shots.line: Double your weight, and you sink like a stone.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: the 2× body sinks

shots.line: Archimedes figured that out more than two thousand years ago.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: Archimedes outline in a bath, ~250 BC; REAL

shots.line: The heavier something is, the harder it presses on the ground, and the harder it is to drag.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: weight arrow down, friction arrow back

shots.line: That's friction.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: FRICTION label

shots.line: It's why the truck couldn't move you.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: the truck pulls, you don't move

shots.line: And every object pulls on every other object.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: two balls pulling each other

shots.line: Right now, you're pulling on your phone.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: you and your phone, tiny arrows

shots.line: Just very, very weakly.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: a magnifier on the tiny arrow

shots.line: In 1798, Henry Cavendish measured that pull between lead balls, in a shed.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: Cavendish's torsion balance in a shed; 1798; REAL

shots.line: Make yourself heavy enough, and that tiny pull gets big.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: the arrows grow huge

shots.line: And astronauts don't float because there's no gravity up there.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: an astronaut in orbit, gravity arrow still there

shots.line: They float because they're falling around the Earth, all the time.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: Newton's cannon, the ball falls around the Earth

shots.scene: arrows: everything loose drifts toward you

shots.line: Toward you.
shots.scene: BIG FACE: eyes wide
